speaker: Doctor
text: I need to ask some questions to understand the newborn's condition better. Since the baby is a newborn, I will ask the parents about the symptoms. How long has the baby been having trouble breathing, and was there any trauma during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for those details. Given the prematurity and gestational diabetes, are you noticing any specific signs like grunting, nasal flaring, or retractions? Also, was there any meconium staining of the amniotic fluid during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas (ABG) and Pulse_Oximetry. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray. Please describe the color of the baby's skin and note if there are any crackles heard upon auscultation.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin color shows cyanosis, especially around the lips. No distinct crackles were heard upon auscultation.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Transient Tachypnea of the Newborn (TTN). Given the preterm status, cesarean delivery without labor, and chest X-ray findings of fluid overload without the air bronchograms typical of RDS, this is the most likely diagnosis. Please ensure the baby remains on supplemental oxygen and monitor for rapid improvement.
